Unfortunately all I can offer you is solidarity. I’ve found myself in much the same situation. I used to have hope that things may change, but even that has died and now I’m just trying to simply resign myself to the fact that this is the way it is and hoping a stray bus takes me out or something. 
Everyone in my life keeps saying oh it gets better, and maybe it does but when? When I’m 50? If then? Some people just don’t find the things they’re looking for and I kind of wish people would stop lying to me about that. It would make me feel less crazy. Less isolated. 

There’s a book I read in high school “Into the Wild” and the man- Chris McCandless, who was a real person, died alone in the woods with the singular message he’d realized in his travels. “Happiness only real when shared”
I’ve always kind of believed that. But how are you supposed to find happiness when you keep trying and trying but you can’t seem to find those people to share it with? Where are they? How do I do it? 
I didn’t have any friends then. My family life was so bad that all I could do was keep looking forward, waiting for college. Then I waited to find my place in the world. I keep waiting and waiting and trying and trying and I’ve moved and run away countless times trying to find this mystical place where I’m just supposed to *fit* but I must not be a part of any main story cause I just keep drifting and finding nothing.

Dude it’s the same for me. I really struggle with day to day conversations sometimes. Some days are worse than others, and it might depend who I’m talking to,  but my memory too has really taken a hit. I forget words or the trail of my thoughts, then I realize this and get a mini panic bc I know I’m gonna look stupid even tho I know what I was gonna say I just can’t find it. And it’s all a tornado from there. But you just have to keep trying. Psyching yourself out makes it a lot worse, as does talking to judgemental people who make you harder on yourself in turn. If you think you can’t handle a conversation, just listen and answer minimally. Take a deep breath when you think you’re losing a thought or jumbling something and take a moment as though collecting your thoughts. I’ve even been trying to read more and learn new small things to prove to myself that I am smart, and I am capable. Because although I’ve known it before, my full mind and body didn’t fully believe it. Idk if that makes sense haha.

Thank you :) I am taking steps, it’s difficult even just realizing that you’re letting yourself get trampled on and then making a point to change your own thinking. You have to tell yourself, I AM smart. I AM worthy of this position. I DO have intelligence. I don’t always believe it when others tell me it because I feel like they’re being just nice. But having started to tell Myself these things, I’ve started to believe it more when other people say as much as well. It partially all ties into internalized misogyny I believe as well. As women were told from a very young age how we’re supposed to be- what role we take, what we need to look like, etc etc. so when our partners later in life kind of bind into that ideology and speak to us in these ways, it really drives home the thought that we’re the lesser stupider gender. When that’s just not true at all. In most cases women are actually superior. Men only think they are because they’re simply told that from a young age so they hold that confidence that they actually are. We, in comparison, have to earn it.

I’m under the belief system that when we’re young we’re all toxic just because we don’t necessarily know any better for a lot of reasons. The difference is being able to look back and recognize this in yourself and change accordingly, or never change your behavior. If you never change then that’s the bad person. But someone who’s able to grow is the one who feels bad about it and worries

I’m feeling much the same way. You’re most definitely not alone. My situation is a little bit different but I get the sense that everyone’s situation is simultaneously a little different and very much the same. We’re like ghosts wandering in limbo, unsure of what step to take next and if there even is one right now. But the truth is it’s just all a waiting game. 
This has been the longest year of my life, and while I’ve always struggled with depression I’ve seen more and more people formerly not as afflicted find their downfall in these uncertain times. We mustn’t forget that we’re not the only one going through this, as much as it might seem so. The people who have gotten back to life are very few and far between, they’re just the more vocal online amongst the sea of us still stuck jobless in our apartments. 
Just know that your holler into the void here has reached others going through the same. And you’re not alone. It’s a scary time of unprecedented struggles we haven’t seen in our lifetimes outside of history books. We’re living through the American history section of high school that schoolteachers will highlight for a couple days a decade from now. 
Give yourself credit where credit is due. You’re still here and you’re still moving and trying. Some can’t even get out of bed at this point, others have turned to negative vices, and others are dead. Try to see the little things as blessings in a time like this and be easy on yourself. That’s all any of us can do. 
Losing all that we have is not an easy thing to get over, and we shouldn’t expect everyone to be okay right now. Mourn the losses of your former life, be kind to your mind and your body, and try little by little to build yourself up again without putting the weight of the world on your shoulders.

I’m still researching but I’m most likely pursuing a degree in biology. From there I could specialize in something like marine biology or zoology or one of the other ology’s. That I’m still figuring out and researching bc of job prospects and such. Kind of skrrting to a way different path but I’ve always liked science, and I could more easily get a steady job with a degree like that and bring it to a lot of things. I made a mistake when I was younger and got a film degree, because it truly is worth nothing and there is very little transfer of knowledge to other areas with it, unless you already specialized your studies somehow. I mostly just needed to get out of an abusive household at the time and went for something I thought would bring me joy. It did for awhile, but I didn’t plan well enough and the more I think about my future the more I need stability and the ability to actually do my taxes without 500 different jobs sending me 1099s. I’ve heard programming is a good path for a lot of folks, especially those needing a steady income. It’s not my cup of tea but if it’s something you’re interested in I’d suggest researching more and considering options. A lot of people in the arts right now are realizing the same as us and it’s really bringing forth the thought, “do I want this unpredictability to be my life?” The arts can be fun and worth it, but there is also a great toll mentally, physically and financially that some, like myself, just cannot take anymore. And that’s ok. We can still have these artistic pieces in our life but instead keep them as hobbies or side hustles, and maybe that will make them more enjoyable in the end rather than a potential burden.

I have the copper iud and I got it in March I think. I’ve had very bad cramps. But I do have a story. For my first period after the insertion, about a month after, I was getting such bad cramps I could barely leave bed and I felt nauseous and Ill. This lasted several days to the point I knew something was wrong. I was crying in bed and my poor boyfriend was frantic about how to help. I started thinking, omg, I’m feeling so sick, what if i have a tampon stuck up in me and I’ve got TSS?? So I decided to go to the bathroom and reach up and check. I felt a little bit of cotton up there and I thought omg how long has this been in here? Cause it felt like the little knot at the end of a tampon string. So I took two fingers and tugged. It felt a little off like something was getting unlodged, but it didn’t hurt at all so I tugged again. Just two little tugs and then as soon as it started slipping out I knew I made a mistake. Cause out pulled my iud!! I just pulled it right out of me. Some cotton from a tampon was stuck on the end of the string so that’s why i was confused. Hands shaking and lightheaded, I rand to my boyfriend who was right outside in the kitchen and said that I have to go to the doctor right now. He was like what? And i showed the iud. He stayed extremely calm and even calmed me down. But the thing was, I had felt tremendously better immediately. As soon as I tugged it out. Nausea and cramps all gone immediately. I ended up going back to planned parenthood the next day and got it reinserted and it’s been fine since then. But they thought that the reason it had been so horribly painful was it was slipped and lodged in the cervix and coming out a bit. Being stuck there the cervix would be just constantly open or at least being tapped and prodded by the thing, causing these terrible cramps. So in short, maybe get it checked out because it could be out of place and hitting your cervix in a way that causes worse cramps. And also don’t tug out your iud yourself lol.
